title: Leveraging Omics Data and Large Language Models to Identify Natural Substances Targeting Overexpressed Genes in Psoriasis
content: Background. Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune disease marked by excessive skin cell growth and inflammation, driven by the overexpression of certain key genes. Advances in omics have revealed genes pivotal to psoriasis, while natural substances offer the potential for gene modulation. By combining omics data with large language models (LLMs) driven by artificial intelligence (AI), this study aimed to identify natural substances that can downregulate overexpressed genes, providing a novel approach to treat psoriasis. Method. We retrieved psoriasis microarray data from the National Institutes of Health Gene Expression Omnibus repository (series GSE30999), consisting of 170 skin biopsy samples from 85 patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis who were not undergoing active treatment at the time of collection. For natural substance recommendations, we utilized two LLMs, ChatGPT from OpenAI and Gemini from Google. Results. Our results identified the top 10 overexpressed genes in psoriasis, including S100A12, SERPINB3, S100A7A, and KYNU, using gene expression data from psoriatic skin samples. By integrating these omics data with AI-driven recommendations from LLMs, we were able to propose several natural substances that may target these genes. Notable suggestions included quercetin for S100A12, resveratrol for SERPINB4, and curcumin for S100A7A, though our analysis revealed a lack of direct evidence linking these substances to specific gene modulation. Both ChatGPT and Gemini offered overlapping recommendations, such as curcumin, green tea extract, and resveratrol, suggesting consistency in their potential therapeutic benefits. Additional substances like aloe vera, bromelain, astragalus, omega-3 fatty acids, and ginger were also proposed for their broader anti-inflammatory and dermatological effects. Conclusions. Our study underscores the potential of combining omics data with LLM-driven insights to explore natural treatments for psoriasis. While the proposed natural substances exhibit promise due to their known bioactive properties, a critical need remains for direct evidence linking these substances to specific gene targets. Future research should focus on validating these interactions in experimental settings, which could pave the way for more targeted and effective natural therapies for psoriasis.
